published_hypotheses: UNREAD at source; the hypotheses below are those the formula provably requires (re-derived here), not quoted from Le:
H1 thin (distributional) shell; Einstein equations with the Lanczos/Israel surface stress from the jump [K_ab] (Poisson-Visser eq (8), READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT)
H2 spherical symmetry; interior Minkowski (f=1), exterior Schwarzschild of mass m (f=1-2m/r), normal from inside to outside; 0 < x = 2m/R < 1
H3 STATIC equilibrium Rdot = Rddot = 0 at R = R_0 (the margin is an equilibrium value)
H4 surface stress S^a_b = diag(-sigma, p, p) (Type I, tangentially isotropic); surface dec means sigma >= |p|; with p_0 > 0 (proven, not assumed, for 0<x<1) this is sigma_0 - p_0 >= 0
H5 geometric units G = c = 1; no empirical input enters
hypothesis_drift: SOURCE-SIDE DRIFT UNCHECKABLE: with 2606.22531 unread, no drift between Le's printed hypotheses and the tree's use can be established or excluded. The items below are drifts between the formula's provable hypotheses and the tree's use.

IMPLICIT, not named in the canonical hypotheses -- H3 static equilibrium (wall.py:41-47, 12-14): 'the dec margin is therefore untouched' / 'independent of the equation-of-state slope' is TRUE of the equilibrium margin (sigma_0, p_0 contain no beta^2; C6 here), but off equilibrium the margin moves with beta^2 at first order: d(sigma-p)/dR|_R0 = (1-beta^2)(-2(sigma_0+p_0)/R_0), d/dbeta^2 = (1-s)(3s+1)/(8 pi R^2 s) != 0 (C7). For the oscillating stiff wall wall.py builds (omega = sqrt(V''/2)), the instantaneous margin during an excursion is beta^2-dependent; the decoupling is an equilibrium statement. Not a refutation of wall.py's text, which speaks of the static margin; a hypothesis to name.

EXTERIOR WEAKENED to its static limit (wall.py:83-86 statics(); warpshell.py:18): Le's realized exterior is the Kinnersley photon rocket (outgoing null dust); Eq (17) as reproduced is the non-radiating Minkowski/Schwarzschild junction, i.e. lambda = aR/c^2 = 0. The tree itself records that for the radiating wall the dec window shrinks with lambda: 'lambda <~ (24/25 - x)/2  empirical dec envelope, not an inequality' (warpshell.py:91, 189). So 'no cost in dec margin' (wall.py:12-13) is established here at lambda = 0 only; at lambda > 0 the margin is the tree's empirical envelope, not Eq (17).

WINDOW EDGES (wall.py:47 'surface dec iff x < 24/25'): the margin is zero at s = 1/5 (x = 24/25) and at s = 1 (x = 0, no shell), positive exactly on 0 < x < 24/25 (z3, C5). So STRICT dec iff 0 < x < 24/25; non-strict dec holds on 0 < x <= 24/25. warpshell.py:86 says 'surface dec strict', which is the precise reading. Wording only.

NOT A DRIFT, recorded because the canonical lists it as a hypothesis: 'Type I surface stress with p > 0' (wall.py:258-260) is not an extra assumption -- p_0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R s) > 0 for every 0 < x < 1 (z3, C5).

NOT A DRIFT: the 24/25 thin-shell window is not the operative one; wall.py carries X_TANGENTIAL = 4/5 for the realized tangential-pressure wall (wall.py:244; warpshell.py:87) and correctly records 'the thin-shell dec window 24/25 is NOT' below x* = 0.8437 (wall.py:554).

DISCREPANCY IN THE TREE'S OWN CHECK, recorded not repaired: wall.py:527-528 asserts 'dec margin is identical for every beta^2 (it is junction-fixed)' via len({round(dec_margin_scaled(0.3), 12)}) == 1 -- a one-element set, true for any input; no beta^2 is varied, so the check is vacuous. The claim itself holds structurally (statics() takes no beta^2; C6 here), so nothing it guards is false.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (exit 0). C1: static extrinsic curvature from K_ab = (1/2) L_n g_ab gives K^th_th = 1/R (in), sqrt(1-2m/R)/R (out), K^tau_tau = 0 (in), m/(R^2 sqrt(1-2m/R)) (out). C2: Lanczos gives sigma_0 = (1-s)/(4 pi R), p_0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R s), identical to wall.py statics(). C3: 8 pi R(sigma_0 - p_0) - [-(5s-1)(s-1)/(2s)] simplifies to 0. C4: zeros {1/5, 1}; s = 1/5 <=> x = 24/25, R = 25m/12 > 2m. C5 (z3, quantified over all real s in (0,1), negations unsat, vacuity guards sat): margin > 0 <=> s > 1/5; p_0 > 0 throughout; sigma_0 > 0. C6: with the standard dynamic forms K^th_th = sqrt(f+Rdot^2)/R, K^tau_tau = (Rddot + f'/2)/sqrt(f+Rdot^2), the conservation law d(sigma A)/dtau + p dA/dtau = 0 holds identically and the static reduction returns C2 -- no beta^2 enters sigma_0, p_0. C7: off equilibrium d(sigma-p)/dR|_R0 = (1-beta^2)(-2(sigma_0+p_0)/R_0), beta^2-dependent, zero only at beta^2 = 1. C8: wall.py dec_margin_scaled, dec_margin_le and this file's closed form agree to < 1e-12 at x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 24/25 (wall.py imported read-only, no bytecode written). The formula the tree attributes to Le Eq (17) is therefore CORRECT as mathematics under H1-H5; whether it is what Le printed is unverified.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite on this result as a matter of data: the margin is a closed-form identity of the static Minkowski/Schwarzschild Lanczos junction with no empirical input (data_at_publication), so no datum the authors lacked could move it -- evidence: the re-derivation from the metric alone reproduces it exactly and z3 proves the window on the whole interval. What IS incomplete is scope, not data: (i) it is an equilibrium value -- the margin of an oscillating wall depends on beta^2 at first order (C7); (ii) it is the lambda = 0 (non-radiating) junction, whereas Le's realized exterior radiates and the tree's own empirical envelope lambda <~ (24/25 - x)/2 (warpshell.py:91) says the window shrinks with acceleration. Neither is a missing measurement; both are named hypotheses. The one thing genuinely lacking here is Le's text itself, which could not be read.
grade_evidence: The source, arXiv:2606.22531 Eq (17), could not be read in this stage (alphaXiv quota exceeded on all three tools; arxiv.org refused by the proxy), so the claim 'Le's Eq (17) reads -(5s-1)(s-1)/(2s) with dec iff x < 24/25' is uncheckable here and is OPEN, not flattened to STANDS. Evidence either way on the CONTENT is strong and independent of Le: sympy re-derives 8 pi R(sigma_0 - p_0) = -(5s-1)(s-1)/(2s) from the Lanczos junction built from the metric (C1-C3), z3 proves strict surface dec <=> 0 < x < 24/25 over every real s in (0,1) (C5), and wall.py's numbers agree to < 1e-12 (C8). The tree's dependents -- wall.py's 'dec margin untouched' and 'thin-shell dec window 24/25 is NOT below x*' (wall.py:554) -- rest on the tree's own derivation, which wall.py:269-271 already marks 'never used as a source', so the openness of the attribution does not reach them. Two named hypotheses bound them: static equilibrium (the margin of an excursion is beta^2-dependent, C7) and lambda = 0 (warpshell.py:91's empirical envelope governs the radiating wall). One vacuous self-check is recorded (wall.py:527-528). No refutation, no moved datum.
what_would_change_the_grade: Reading Eq (17) of arXiv:2606.22531 at source: if it prints -(5s-1)(s-1)/(2s) (equivalently (1-s)(5s-1)/(2s)) for the static Minkowski/Schwarzschild shell with dec iff x < 24/25, the grade becomes STANDS (with the two named hypotheses, static equilibrium and lambda = 0, carried as scope notes -- NARROWED only if the tree is shown to apply the 'no cost in dec margin' clause to an off-equilibrium or lambda > 0 wall as if Eq (17) covered it). If Le prints a different form, that is a DISCREPANCY to record (misprint on one side), not WRONG, because the correct form is computed here; WRONG would require the re-derivation above to fail, which it does not.
